storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific failure mode — speed past the evidence — which the audio states but does not picture.
storyboard.claim: Hari sometimes runs past the strict science to keep a victimhood story intact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst narrator facing Johann, one hand raised in a cautioning pause gesture; Johann looks away mid-stride.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the fair counterpoint setup into the direct critique of Hari.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the Tuesday-afternoon slump the narration names, grounding the abstract blame in a body and a phone.
storyboard.claim: The tech-friction link is real, but blaming big tech for every procrastination goes too far.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped at an office desk, glowing phone in hand, an important task ignored beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens the critique: from Hari's overreach to our own overuse of the excuse.

storyboard.addedInformation: The held-but-not-used phone pictures the agency the narration defends: the choice is still in the hand.
storyboard.claim: Total structural blame strips away the agency to simply put the phone down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding the glowing phone out at arm's length, staring at it instead of using it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Consequence of the previous beat: blame-everything costs us the one move we still own.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pause between pull and swipe is staged as a visible hesitation the audio only describes.
storyboard.claim: However powerful the hijack design, a small gap survives between the pull and the swipe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close on Everyman, finger hovering above the glowing screen, hesitating instead of swiping.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the algorithm's power while opening the gap the close will build on.

storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the abstract 'own it' into a pointed finger at the hovering hand — responsibility plus resistance.
storyboard.claim: We must own that gap even while fighting the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing at his own hovering finger above the phone while the narrator faces him, underscoring the choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the gap's existence to the demand: occupy it, starting tomorrow.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the denial visibly: no lost keys, no slumped lazy figure — an upright reader facing a theft, not a misplacement.
storyboard.claim: Attention was not lost or lazily misplaced; it was stolen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sitting upright in a dark bedroom, phone face-down, staring straight ahead as the verdict lands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Hard turn from agency back to the book's core verdict: this part is not your fault.

storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer strings picture the 'systematically' the audio asserts — control from far away, drawn literally.
storyboard.claim: The theft is systematic: your exhaustion converted into someone else's quarterly revenue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The puppeteer icon looming over a slumped Everyman, strings running from the controller's hands to his glowing phone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the theft verdict into its motive: profit.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone held loosely at the side, gaze lifted off it, pictures the trance broken that the narration describes.
storyboard.claim: Stolen things can be taken back — the shift from despair to action.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman surfacing from a scroll, phone lowered, eyes lifting with a dawning alertness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The paradigm pivot: from the theft and its motive to the possibility of return.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strings made visible turn the listener's self-question into something to see: whose hand moves yours?
storyboard.claim: Ask whether this scroll is your free choice or a boardroom-engineered extraction of your life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The puppeteer icon's strings reaching toward Everyman's eyes and phone as he looks up, questioning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the take-back personal: the test question for the next trance moment.

storyboard.addedInformation: The raised phone-free hand stages refusal as a shared physical act, not a slogan — together, hands empty.
storyboard.claim: Together, we can simply refuse to hand our attention over.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman and the narrator side by side, hands raised and empty, phones down, in open collective refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the arc: from critique through theft to the joint refusal that answers it.
